# Show agents what other work touches their paths

## Intent

When many agents work on one repository, the expensive conflicts are the ones nobody saw coming. This package makes in-flight work visible early: before an agent starts it can ask who else touches the paths it is about to edit and announce its own plan as an expiring claim, and while it works it is told when another change starts to touch the files of its own change. Awareness is advisory: it informs, and it never refuses a push, a commit or a land.

## Goals

- `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/activity` answers, for a list of path globs and a target branch, with the `draft` and `open` changes that touch a matching file, the active claims whose globs can match the same files, and the changes that landed on the target since a commit or a time.
- `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/overlaps` lists every other `draft` or `open` change with the same target branch and at least one touched file in common, largest overlap first.
- The hub keeps, per workspace and target branch, the full set of files each change touches, and brings it up to date after each new version, retarget, land, abandon and restore, without delaying the request that caused the update.
- When two changes start to overlap, each gets exactly one `parley.change.overlap` event naming the other; the pair is announced again only after it stopped overlapping.
- A claim is created, read, listed, renewed and released through five routes; creating one returns the current activity for its paths in the same answer.
- A claim expires by itself at `expires_at`, is linked to the change its session opens, becomes `fulfilled` when that change lands or is abandoned, and is removed 7 days after it ended.
- `parley activity`, `parley change overlaps` and `parley claim create|list|renew|release` drive those routes, and `--fail-on-overlap` exits 3 when something overlaps.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Changes and their store arrive with package 22 in `internal/change/`; the event component with package 52 in `internal/event/`; the access component with package 07 in `internal/access/`; the router, error envelope and list helpers with package 02 in `internal/server/`; the configuration loader, the store, background work and the maintenance loop with package 03; the git wrapper in `internal/gitrepo/`; the CLI root, HTTP client and exit codes with package 09 in `internal/cli/`.

## Requirements

### Access and addressing (AWR-FR-001)

All routes are under `/api/v1/workspaces/:slug`. The four reads (`GET …/activity`, `GET …/changes/:number/overlaps`, `GET …/claims`, `GET …/claims/:id`) need the scope `changes:read` from a PAT and read access to the workspace. The three claim writes (`POST …/claims`, `PATCH …/claims/:id`, `DELETE …/claims/:id`) need `changes:write` and read access: claims change nothing in the repository, so an org member may make them (PLAT-FR-062). A PAT without the scope gets `403 insufficient_scope`; a caller without read access gets `404 not_found`, the same answer as for an unknown slug.

Through a task fork's slug the routes act on the fork's parent: access is decided on the fork, and the activity, the overlaps, the change numbers and the claims are the parent's. A claim made through a fork's slug is stored on the parent and carries the parent's slug in `workspace_slug`.

A claim can be renewed, edited and released by its creator (the user behind the credential that made it, with any credential of that user), by the owner of the workspace the claim is stored on, and by the admin token. Any other reader gets `403 forbidden` and the claim is unchanged. A claim id that names no claim of the addressed workspace is `404` with `error_type` `claim_not_found`.

The routes have no state precondition: they answer in every workspace status.

### The overlap index (§9.7, AWR-FR-006, §9.10)

The hub keeps, per workspace and target branch, which `draft` and `open` changes touch which files. A change's files are those that differ between the `base_sha` and the `head_sha` of its current version; a renamed file counts under both of its paths. A change touching more than 2,000 files is indexed in full; only lists returned to clients are capped. Landed changes stay in the index, marked as landed with their landed commit and time, so that activity can report them.

The index is updated after each new version, retarget, land, abandon and restore. The update is asynchronous: the push, commit or API call that caused it is answered without waiting for it, and a failure of the update never changes that answer. The update is durable: after a restart the hub continues where it stopped and announces no overlap twice. If the files of a version cannot be listed (its commits are gone after a reclone), the change is recorded with no files and the work continues with the next change.

### Overlaps of a change (AWR-FR-004, §9.3)

Two changes overlap when both are `draft` or `open`, have the same target branch and have at least one touched file in common. Changes in one stack (linked through `depends_on`, directly or through other changes) do not overlap each other. Overlap is on file paths, not on lines: two changes that edit different functions of one file overlap.

`GET …/changes/:number/overlaps` answers `200` with a list (`items`, `next_cursor`) of overlap entries, one for every other change that overlaps this one, ordered by `count` descending, then `number` ascending. For a change that is `landed` or `abandoned` the list is empty. A number that names no change of the workspace is `404` with `error_type` `change_not_found`.

An overlap entry has `change` (a summary: `number`, `ref`, `title`, `intent` cut to its first 500 characters, `state`, `author`, `session_id`, `version`, `updated_at`, `mergeable`, and `landing` with `status`), `paths` (the files in common in ascending order, at most 100), `paths_truncated` (true when there are more than 100) and `count` (the number of files in common).

### Overlap events (AWR-FR-005, §9.8)

When an index update makes two changes overlap that did not overlap before, the hub emits one `parley.change.overlap` for each of the two, naming the other. The event has `resource_type` `change`, `resource_id` the change number, the target workspace as `workspace`, the actor `system`, the change's own `session_id`, and metadata `number`, `with` (`number` and `ref` of the other change), `with_session_id`, `paths` (at most 100) and `count`. The pair is announced once: further versions that keep the two overlapping emit nothing. When they stop overlapping (no common file any more, different targets, or one of them landed or abandoned) the pair is forgotten, and a later overlap is announced again.

### Activity (AWR-FR-002, AWR-FR-003)

`GET …/activity` takes `paths` (required: one or more globs, as a comma list, repeated, or both; at most 50), `target` (default: the default branch of the workspace acted on), `since`, `exclude_session` and `exclude_change`. It answers `200` with:

- `target_branch` and `target_sha` (the head of that branch, or `null` when the workspace has no such branch);
- `changes`: the `draft` and `open` changes on that target with a touched file matching any glob, as overlap entries whose `paths` and `count` are the matching files, ordered by `count` descending, then `number` ascending;
- `claims`: the active claims on that target with a glob that can match the same files as a requested glob, newest first. Two globs are treated as matching when either one, used as a pattern, matches the other's literal prefix (its text before the first `*`); this errs on the side of reporting;
- `landed`: the changes landed on that target after `since` that touched a matching file, newest first, at most 100, each `{number, ref, title, landed_sha, landed_at, session_id, paths}`.

`since` is a full 40-character commit id (typically the caller's fork point or base: the changes whose landed commit is not reachable from it are reported) or an RFC 3339 timestamp (the changes landed after it). Its default is 24 hours before the request.

With `exclude_session=<id>` the changes, claims and landed changes of that session are left out; with `exclude_change=<number>` that change and the claims linked to it are left out.

Errors, all `400 invalid_request`: `paths` missing or empty; more than 50 globs; a glob that is empty, longer than 255 characters or starts with `/`; a `since` that is neither a 40-character commit id nor a timestamp, or a commit id the repository does not hold; an `exclude_change` that is not a positive integer.

Activity shows changes whose source is a fork the caller cannot read; the change lives in the target workspace, which the caller can read. Drafts are included.

### Claims (AWR-FR-007, AWR-FR-008, AWR-FR-010, AWR-FR-011, §9.3)

A claim has `id` (UUID), `workspace_slug`, `paths` (1–50 globs), `target_branch`, `intent` (1–2,000 characters), `by` (`{actor_type, actor_id, username}`), `session_id` (string or null), `change` (int or null), `expires_at`, `state` (`active`, `released`, `expired`, `fulfilled`) and `created_at`.

`POST …/claims` takes `{"paths", "intent", "target_branch"?, "ttl"?, "session_id"?}`. `target_branch` defaults to the default branch of the workspace acted on; `ttl` defaults to `[awareness].default_claim_ttl` and may not exceed `[awareness].max_claim_ttl`. The answer is `201 {"claim": <claim>, "activity": <the activity answer for the claim's paths and target, without the claim itself>}`, and `parley.claim.create` is emitted (`resource_type` `claim`, `resource_id` the id, `workspace` the workspace the claim is stored on, the caller as actor, metadata `paths`, `intent`, `target_branch`, `expires_at`). Claims never conflict with each other: two sessions may claim the same paths, and each sees the other in the activity. A claim on paths that do not exist yet is valid.

Errors: `400 invalid_request` for an invalid body (`paths` not an array of 1–50 strings, a glob that is empty, longer than 255 characters or starts with `/`, `intent` missing or outside 1–2,000 characters, `ttl` not a duration, not positive or above the maximum, `target_branch` empty or longer than 255 characters); `400 unknown_session` when `session_id` fails the session-linking rule of §14; `429` with `error_type` `claim_limit_reached` when the workspace already has `[awareness].max_claims_per_workspace` active claims or the session already has 50. A refused request stores nothing and emits nothing.

`GET …/claims` lists claims newest first with the filters `state` (default `active`), `session_id` and `path` (a glob, matched by the rule above), paged with `limit` and `cursor`. `GET …/claims/:id` reads one.

`PATCH …/claims/:id` takes `{"ttl"?, "intent"?}`: `ttl` moves `expires_at` to the time of the request plus `ttl` (at most the maximum), `intent` replaces the intent. It answers `200` with the claim. A claim that is not active is `409` with `error_type` `claim_not_active`. A body with neither member, or an invalid one, is `400 invalid_request`.

`DELETE …/claims/:id` releases an active claim: its state becomes `released`, `parley.claim.release` is emitted (metadata `paths`, the caller as actor) and the answer is `204`. Releasing a claim that is not active is a no-op that also answers `204` and emits nothing.

Claims have no effect on pushes, commits, policy or landing.

### Claim lifetime (AWR-FR-008, AWR-FR-009, §9.7)

A claim past its `expires_at` counts as `expired` at once in every read and in the limits. Every minute the hub marks such claims `expired` in the store and emits `parley.claim.expire` for each (actor `system`, metadata `paths`).

When a change is opened with a `session_id` that has active claims on the same workspace and target branch, those claims get `change` set to its number. When that change lands or is abandoned, its claims that are still active become `fulfilled`.

A claim that is `released`, `expired` or `fulfilled` is kept for 7 days and then removed by the `claim_cleanup` task of the hourly maintenance loop.

### Configuration (§9.9)

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[awareness].default_claim_ttl` | duration | `1h` | TTL of a claim without `ttl` |
| `[awareness].max_claim_ttl` | duration | `24h` | Longest TTL |
| `[awareness].max_claims_per_workspace` | int | `1000` | Active claims per workspace |

A duration that is not positive, a default above the maximum, or a claim limit below 1 stops the start with an error naming the key.

### CLI (§9.6)

- `parley activity <slug>` with `--paths <list>` (required), `--target <branch>`, `--since <sha|time>`, `--exclude-session <id>`, `--exclude-change <number>`, `--fail-on-overlap`: calls `GET …/activity`.
- `parley change overlaps <slug> <number>` with `--fail-on-overlap`: calls `GET …/changes/:number/overlaps`.
- `parley claim create <slug>` with `--paths <list>` (required), `--intent <text>` (required), `--target <branch>`, `--ttl <duration>`, `--session <id>`: calls `POST …/claims`.
- `parley claim list <slug>` with `--state`, `--session`, `--path`, `--limit`, `--cursor`: calls `GET …/claims`.
- `parley claim renew <slug> <id>` with `--ttl <duration>` (default `1h`): calls `PATCH …/claims/:id`.
- `parley claim release <slug> <id>`: calls `DELETE …/claims/:id` and prints `{}`.

Each command prints the route's response body and exits by the global rules. With `--fail-on-overlap` the result is printed first; then, when `changes` or `claims` of the activity answer (or `items` of the overlaps answer) is not empty, `condition_not_met` is reported on stderr and the exit status is 3. A missing required flag, a wrong number of arguments or a number that is not a positive integer is a usage error (exit status 2) and no request is sent.

### End-to-end flows

**Two agents meet on one file.** An agent opens change 1 from a branch that edits `api/handler.go`. A second agent runs `parley claim create demo --paths 'api/**' --intent "rework handlers" --session <id>`; the parley CLI posts the claim; `parleyd` stores it, emits `parley.claim.create` and answers with the claim and an activity that lists change 1. The second agent goes on anyway and opens change 2, which edits the same file; `parleyd` accepts it, the claim gets `change: 2`, the index worker records both changes and emits one `parley.change.overlap` on each. The first agent runs `parley change overlaps demo 1 --fail-on-overlap`, reads the entry for change 2 and gets exit status 3.

**A crashed agent's claim disappears.** An agent creates a claim with a `ttl` of 5 minutes and stops. Six minutes later `parleyd`'s expiry run marks the claim `expired` and emits `parley.claim.expire`; activity for the same paths no longer returns it. Seven days later the maintenance loop removes the record.

## Design Decisions

1. **Profile: full.** Two end-to-end flows cross the CLI, the router, the store, the event log and the git wrapper.
2. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; embedded SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` behind `internal/store`; `net/http` with its method-and-pattern router; `github.com/spf13/cobra` for the CLI; git through the `git` binary behind `internal/gitrepo`; the standard `testing` package with table-driven tests, `net/http/httptest` and repositories made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`; a replaceable clock.
3. **The index follows the event log.** A background worker reads the event log in sequence order with `ReadAfter(position, limit)` of the event component of package 52 (`internal/event`), which returns the events after a position and the position up to which the log was examined, starting after a position it stores in the transactional store. It acts on the types `parley.change.version` (which also carries retargets), `parley.change.land`, `parley.change.abandon` and `parley.change.restore`, skips every other type, and moves its position to the examined one. The index update, the overlap events it causes, the claim links and the new position are written in one transaction. Why: it is asynchronous by construction (AWR-FR-006), survives restarts without announcing twice, and needs no call from packages 22, 23 and 25 into this one. The worker looks for new events every second; the PRD gives no latency figure.
4. **Narrow interfaces instead of imports.** `internal/awareness` defines the three things it needs from others as interfaces that `parleyd` wires: an event source, whose one method has the shape of `ReadAfter(position, limit)` of package 52 so that the event component satisfies it as it is; a change reader (one change by workspace and number, with state, target branch, `depends_on`, session, version, `base_sha`, `head_sha`, landed commit and time, and the summary fields), which the exported read of the change component of package 22 implements; and a session interface with two operations, check and record, which package 49 installs from the linking check and the recording operation that `internal/session` exports. Why: the three owners export these under their own names, and `internal/awareness` stays testable with fixtures. With no session interface installed, every `session_id` is refused with `unknown_session`.
5. **A change's files are computed here, not taken from the change's `paths`.** `paths` is capped at 2,000; the index is not (§9.10). The files come from one name-and-status diff with rename detection between `base_sha` and `head_sha`.
6. **Stack membership is read at evaluation time**, by following `depends_on` to the bottom change; two changes with the same bottom are one stack. It is not stored in the index, so a `depends_on` edit needs no index update.
7. **Any index update can announce.** A retarget or a restore that makes two changes overlap is announced like a new version. Why: §9.8 words the event as "two changes started to overlap", and the pair record must agree with the index whatever caused the update.
8. **Order and caps the PRD leaves open.** Equal `count` is ordered by `number` ascending. `paths` in an entry, in an event and in a `landed` item are in ascending byte order and cut to 100. The overlaps list is paged by the list conventions; `changes` and `claims` of the activity answer are not paged and not capped.
9. **`target` is not validated.** An unknown branch gives `target_sha: null` and, normally, empty lists; a claim may name a branch that does not exist yet. Why: awareness is advisory and a claim on paths that do not exist yet is valid (§9.10).
10. **Activity and the claim lists are limited to the target branch**, because the index is kept per target branch (§9.7).
11. **Through a fork's slug the default target is the parent's default branch**, not the fork's base branch. Why: §9.3 says "default: the default branch".
12. **`since` forms.** Exactly 40 hexadecimal characters is a commit id; anything else must parse as an RFC 3339 timestamp. A commit id selects the landed changes whose `landed_sha` is not reachable from it.
13. **A claim is expired from `expires_at` on**, also before the minute's run has written the state: reads report `expired`, activity leaves it out, the limits do not count it, `PATCH` answers `claim_not_active`. The event follows with the run. Why: the acceptance criterion (§16, 11) expects activity to stop returning the claim when it expires.
14. **Limits.** The workspace limit counts active claims stored on the workspace (for a fork: its parent). The session limit of 50 counts active claims that carry that `session_id`; a claim without a session counts for no session. The refusal is `429` with `error_type` `claim_limit_reached`, a type of its own like the other quantity limits of the product (`fork_limit_reached`, `secret_limit_reached`, `sandbox_capacity`); `rate_limited` stays the answer of the request rate limits of package 02 alone. AWR-FR-011 fixes the status and names no type.
15. **`ttl` bounds.** At least 1 second, at most `[awareness].max_claim_ttl`; a renewal without `ttl` leaves `expires_at` alone.
16. **Renewal emits no event**; §9.8 lists none.
17. **Linking a claim to a change** happens when the worker processes the first version of a change (`version` 1) that carries a session: every active claim of that session on the same workspace and target branch whose `change` is null gets the number. A restored change does not turn its `fulfilled` claims back.
18. **`fulfilled` claims are removed like the others**, 7 days after they became `fulfilled`. The store keeps the time a claim ended for this; it is not part of the claim object.
19. **A fork-bound token may read the overlaps of any change of the parent**, not only of its own changes. Why: AWR-FR-001 lists the route without the restriction CHG-FR-040 puts on the change routes, and activity shows the same changes.
20. **No state precondition.** The routes answer in every workspace status, also on an archived workspace: they neither read nor write the repository's branches, except for `target_sha` (null when unreadable) and a commit `since` (`400` when the commit cannot be resolved).
21. **A malformed claim id or change number is "not found"** (`404 claim_not_found`, `404 change_not_found`), not `400`.

## Glossary

- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch. Every push, API commit or restack that moves the source creates a new version.
- **Intent**: The author's statement of why the change exists.
- **Stack**: Changes linked by `depends_on`, lowest first.
- **Claim**: An advisory, expiring statement that a session intends to work on some paths.
- **Session**: An agent session: who ran, on which workspace, with what token usage, and which changes it produced.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Overlap**: Two `draft` or `open` changes with the same target branch and at least one touched file in common, not in one stack.
- **Overlap entry**: The summary of another change together with the files in common and their count.
- **Activity**: The answer to "what touches these paths": in-flight changes, live claims and recently landed changes, each matched against a list of path globs.
- **Literal prefix**: The text of a glob before its first `*`.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Access and addressing of the awareness routes

**Rationale:** An agent that holds only a fork must be able to see and announce work on the parent, and an org member must be able to claim, without either gaining any write to the repository.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any request to GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/activity, GET …/changes/{number}/overlaps, GET …/claims or GET …/claims/{id}, require the scope changes:read from a PAT caller and the access need read on the workspace named by the slug, in the hub's order of checks
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope for a PAT without changes:read or changes:write, whether or not the workspace exists; HTTP 404 with error_type not_found, byte-identical to the answer for an unknown slug, for a caller without read access; otherwise the route's own answer
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace demo in an organization with an owner and one other member, one open change 1 and one active claim, served through the real router, scope check and access component
   ```
   in internal/awareness/routes_test.go, a table over the four read routes and the callers {PAT with only git:read -> 403 insufficient_scope, the same PAT on an unknown slug -> 403 insufficient_scope, user outside the organization -> 404 not_found, member of the organization with an API key -> 200, owner with a PAT holding changes:read -> 200, admin token -> 200}: r = do(route, caller); assert r.status and r.json.error.error_type as listed; assert the stranger's body equals the body for the slug 'no-such-workspace'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any request to POST …/claims, PATCH …/claims/{id} or DELETE …/claims/{id}, require the scope changes:write from a PAT caller and the access need read, so that a member of the workspace's organization may create, renew and release claims
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope for a PAT that holds changes:read but not changes:write; HTTP 404 not_found for a caller without read access; HTTP 201 for a member's valid POST
   Check: integration
   - setup: the workspace demo of the read-route table
   ```
   in internal/awareness/routes_test.go, a table over the three write routes and the callers {PAT with only changes:read -> 403 insufficient_scope, user outside the organization -> 404 not_found, member with an API key -> POST 201, then PATCH 200 and DELETE 204 on the member's own claim}: assert the status and error_type as listed; assert the claim table is unchanged after each refusal
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN an awareness route is addressed with the slug of a task fork, THE parleyd SHALL decide access on the fork and serve the route on the data of the fork's parent: the parent's index, change numbers and claims, with a new claim stored on the parent

### REQ-2: Overlap index of changes by touched file

**Rationale:** Activity and overlaps must answer from a complete picture of which in-flight change touches which file, and keeping that picture must never slow down the push that changes it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the index worker reads a parley.change.version event (a new version or a retarget) of a change, THE parleyd SHALL record the change in the index under its workspace and current target branch as in flight, with the complete set of files that differ between the base_sha and the head_sha of its current version, replacing the set recorded before, counting a renamed file under both its old and its new path and applying no limit to the number of files
   → the index holds exactly the files of the current version for the change; a version touching 2,001 files is recorded with 2,001 files
   Check: integration
   - setup: an event source and a change reader backed by fixtures, the real git wrapper and a real SQLite store
   ```
   in internal/awareness/index_test.go, with a real repository made by git init in t.TempDir(): version 1 edits c.go and renames a.go to b.go; run one worker pass; assert files(index, demo, 1) == {a.go, b.go, c.go}; version 2 edits only d.go on the same base; run a pass; assert files == {d.go}; a retarget event to branch release; run a pass; assert target(index, demo, 1) == 'release'; a change whose version adds 2,001 files; run a pass; assert len(files) == 2001
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN the index worker reads a parley.change.land, parley.change.abandon or parley.change.restore event of a change, THE parleyd SHALL on land mark the change as landed with its landed commit and landing time and keep its files; on abandon take the change out of the in-flight set; on restore put it back in flight with the files of its current version
   → a landed or abandoned change appears in no overlaps list and in no changes list of an activity answer; a landed change appears in landed; a restored change appears in both again
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/index_test.go: changes 1 and 2 in flight on main, both touching api/a.go; feed abandon(2); pass; assert inFlight(index, demo, 'main') == [1]; feed restore(2); pass; assert inFlight(index, demo, 'main') == [1, 2] and files(index, demo, 2) == {api/a.go}; feed land(2) with landed_sha S and landed_at T; pass; assert inFlight(index, demo, 'main') == [1]; assert landed(index, demo, 'main') == [{number: 2, landed_sha: S, landed_at: T}] and files(index, demo, 2) == {api/a.go}
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any push, commit or API call that creates a version or changes a change's state, answer it without waiting for the index update, and update the index later from the event log
   → the request's status and body are the same with the index worker stopped as with it running; the index holds the change only after a worker pass
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub assembled in-process with the real change routes of package 22, the real event log and the awareness worker under manual control
   ```
   in internal/awareness/worker_test.go: with no worker running, r = POST /workspaces/demo/changes for a branch touching api/a.go; assert r.status == 201; assert inFlight(index, demo, 'main') == []; run one worker pass; assert inFlight(index, demo, 'main') == [r.json.number]; assert files(index, demo, r.json.number) == {api/a.go}
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any event it processes, write the index update, the overlap events and claim updates it causes and the position of the event in one transaction, and after a restart continue with the first event after the stored position
   → each event is applied exactly once: after a restart in the middle of a backlog the index and the stored position equal those of an uninterrupted run, and nothing an event caused is written twice
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/worker_test.go: feed five version events for changes 1 and 2; process the first two; close and reopen the store; build a new worker; run passes until idle; assert position(worker) == seq of the fifth event; assert the index equals the index of a run without the restart; assert the fixture change reader was asked for each of the five events once; make the transaction of one further event fail once (a store that returns an error at commit); assert the stored position did not advance and the index is unchanged; run a pass; assert the event is applied
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF the files of a change's current version cannot be listed because a commit of the version is not in the repository or the git command fails, THEN THE parleyd SHALL record the change with an empty set of files, log the failure with the workspace and the change number, advance past the event and continue with the next event
   → the worker pass returns no error and processes the following events; the change appears in no overlap entry; no parley.change.overlap is emitted for it
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/index_test.go: feed a version event of change 3 whose head_sha is 40 zeros, followed by a version event of change 4; err = pass(); assert err == nil; assert files(index, demo, 3) == {}; assert files(index, demo, 4) is not empty; assert position(worker) == seq of the second event
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN parleyd starts, THE parleyd SHALL register the index worker as background work that looks for new events every second until shutdown, and stop it within its grace when the hub shuts down
   → a version recorded while the hub runs is in the index at most one worker interval plus one pass later; after shutdown no pass is running
   Check: same as PATH-1

### REQ-3: Overlaps of a change

**Rationale:** A developer deciding the order in which changes should land needs, for one change, every other in-flight change that touches the same files.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a caller sends GET …/changes/{number}/overlaps for a change in state draft or open, THE parleyd SHALL return one overlap entry for every other draft or open change of the workspace that has the same target branch and at least one indexed file in common with it, ordered by count descending and then by number ascending, as a list paged by limit and cursor
   → HTTP 200 with body {items: [overlap entry…], next_cursor: string or null}
   Check: unit
   - setup: index: change 1 (open, main) touches a, b, c, d; change 2 (draft, main) touches a; change 3 (open, main) touches a, b, c; change 4 (open, main) touches d; change 5 (open, release) touches a; change 6 (abandoned, main) touches a; change 7 (open, main) touches z

   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any two changes in one stack, that is two changes that reach the same bottom change by following depends_on, treat them as not overlapping whatever files they share
   → neither change appears in the other's overlaps list and no parley.change.overlap is emitted for the pair
   Check: unit

   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any overlap entry, return change as the summary {number, ref, title, intent cut to its first 500 characters, state, author, session_id, version, updated_at, mergeable, landing: {status}}, paths as the files in common in ascending byte order cut to the first 100, paths_truncated as true exactly when there are more than 100 files in common, and count as the number of files in common
   → overlap entry: {change: {number: int, ref: string, title: string, intent: string of at most 500 characters, state: string, author: object, session_id: string or null, version: int, updated_at: timestamp, mergeable: string, landing: {status: string}}, paths: string[] of at most 100, paths_truncated: bool, count: int}

   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] WHEN a caller sends GET …/changes/{number}/overlaps for a change in state landed or abandoned, THE parleyd SHALL return an empty list

   Check: unit
   ```

   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] IF the number in GET …/changes/{number}/overlaps names no change of the workspace the route acts on, or is not a positive integer, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 404 with error_type change_not_found
   Check: unit

### REQ-4: Overlap events

**Rationale:** An agent that is already working must be told when another change starts to touch its files, once, without polling.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN an index update makes two changes overlap for which no announced pair is recorded, THE parleyd SHALL emit one parley.change.overlap event for each of the two changes, naming the other, and record the pair as announced, in the transaction of the index update
   → two events of type parley.change.overlap, each with resource_type change, resource_id the change's number as a decimal string, workspace the target workspace, actor system, session_id the session of the change it is written on, and metadata {number, with: {number, ref} of the other change, with_session_id: the other change's session or null, paths: the files in common in ascending order cut to 100, count}
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real event log on SQLite and the index worker under manual control
   ```
   in internal/awareness/overlap_events_test.go: change 1 (session s1) touches api/a.go and api/b.go; feed version 1 of change 2 (session s2) touching api/a.go and x.go; pass; ev = events of type parley.change.overlap; assert len(ev) == 2; e1 = the one with resource_id '1'; assert e1.actor.actor_type == 'system'; assert e1.session_id == s1; assert e1.metadata == {number: 1, with: {number: 2, ref: 'demo#2'}, with_session_id: s2, paths: ['api/a.go'], count: 1}; assert the event with resource_id '2' names {number: 1, ref: 'demo#1'} and with_session_id s1; a pair with 150 common files has metadata.count == 150 and len(metadata.paths) == 100
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHILE a pair of changes is recorded as announced and an index update leaves the two overlapping, THE parleyd SHALL emit no further parley.change.overlap for the pair
   → the number of parley.change.overlap events for the pair stays 2 however many versions either change gets
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/overlap_events_test.go: after the announcement of changes 1 and 2, feed versions 2, 3 and 4 of change 2, each touching api/a.go and a different second file; pass; assert count(events of type parley.change.overlap) == 2; close and reopen the store, build a new worker, feed version 5 of change 2 touching api/a.go; pass; assert the count is still 2
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN an index update leaves an announced pair without a file in common, with different target branches, or with one of the two changes landed or abandoned, THE parleyd SHALL forget the pair, so that a later index update that makes the two overlap is announced again with two new events
   → after the two stop overlapping and overlap again, four parley.change.overlap events exist for the pair in total
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/overlap_events_test.go, a table over the way the pair stops {a version of change 2 that no longer touches api/a.go, a retarget of change 2 to release, abandon of change 2} followed by the way it returns {a version touching api/a.go again, a retarget back to main, restore}: after the stop assert count(overlap events) == 2 and pairs(index) == []; after the return assert count == 4
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHEN one index update makes a change overlap several other changes at once, THE parleyd SHALL announce each new pair separately
   → 2 × k events for k new pairs: one on the updated change per partner and one on each partner
   Check: integration
   ```

   ```

### REQ-6: Claim creation

**Rationale:** An agent must be able to announce what it is about to work on before it has any code, and learn in the same call who is already there.

#### Criteria

[REQ-6.1] WHEN a caller sends POST …/claims with a valid body, THE parleyd SHALL store a claim with a new UUID as id, the slug of the workspace the route acts on, the given paths and intent, target_branch as given or else that workspace's default branch, by as the caller's actor type, id and username, session_id as given or null, change null, state active, created_at the time of the request and expires_at that time plus ttl or, without ttl, plus [awareness].default_claim_ttl; emit parley.claim.create in the same transaction; and answer with the claim and the activity for the claim's paths and target branch without the claim itself
   → HTTP 201 with body {claim: {id, workspace_slug, paths, target_branch, intent, by: {actor_type, actor_id, username}, session_id, change, expires_at, state, created_at}, activity: {target_branch, target_sha, changes, claims, landed}}; one event parley.claim.create with resource_type claim, resource_id the id, workspace the claim's workspace_slug, the caller as actor and metadata {paths, intent, target_branch, expires_at}
   Check: integration
   - setup: workspace demo with default branch main and an open change 1 touching api/a.go in the index
   - setup: [awareness] at its defaults
   - setup: a real event log on SQLite

1. [REQ-6.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any claim, accept it whatever other claims exist on the same or intersecting paths, and show each of two such claims in the other's activity

   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; the number of stored claims is unchanged; a body with 50 globs, an intent of 2,000 characters and a ttl equal to the maximum is answered 201

[REQ-6.4] IF the session_id of POST …/claims fails the session-linking rule: the session does not exist, was created by another user while the caller is not the admin token, or belongs to a workspace that is neither the addressed workspace nor its parent nor one of its forks, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and store nothing

   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] IF POST …/claims arrives while the workspace the claim would be stored on already has [awareness].max_claims_per_workspace active claims, or while the session named by session_id already has 50 active claims, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and store nothing, counting only claims in state active that are not past their expires_at
   → HTTP 429 with error_type claim_limit_reached; the number of stored claims is unchanged
   Check: unit

   ```

### REQ-7: Reading, renewing and releasing claims

**Rationale:** Long tasks renew their claim, finished ones release it, and everyone can see which claims are live.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a caller sends GET …/claims/{id} for a claim stored on the workspace the route acts on, THE parleyd SHALL return the claim, reporting the state expired for a claim that is stored as active and whose expires_at is not after the time of the request
   → HTTP 200 with the claim object of eleven members; state is one of active, released, expired, fulfilled
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_routes_test.go: create a claim with ttl '5m' at T; r = GET …/claims/{id} at T + 4m59s; assert r.status == 200 and r.json.state == 'active'; at T + 5m without running the expiry assert r.json.state == 'expired'; assert keys(r.json) == the eleven members
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN a caller sends GET …/claims, THE parleyd SHALL return the claims stored on the workspace the route acts on that are in the state given by state (default active), carry the session given by session_id when present and have a glob able to match the same files as the glob given by path when present, ordered by created_at descending and then id descending, paged by limit and cursor
   → HTTP 200 with body {items: [claim…], next_cursor: string or null}; HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request for a state other than active, released, expired or fulfilled
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_routes_test.go: claims A (active, s1, ['api/**']), B (active, s2, ['docs/**']) created later, C (released, s1, ['api/**']), D (active by state but past expires_at); a table {no query -> [B, A]; state=released -> [C]; state=expired -> [D]; session_id=s1 -> [A]; path=api/v1/*.go -> [A]; state=fulfilled -> []; limit=1 -> [B] with a next_cursor whose page is [A]; state=bogus -> 400 invalid_request}: assert ids(items) or the error as listed
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN a permitted caller sends PATCH …/claims/{id} for an active claim with ttl, intent or both, THE parleyd SHALL with ttl set expires_at to the time of the request plus ttl, with intent replace the intent, leave every other member unchanged, emit no event and return the claim
   → HTTP 200 with the updated claim object
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_routes_test.go with the clock at T + 30m for a claim created at T with the default ttl, a table {ttl: '2h' -> expires_at == T + 2h30m, intent unchanged; intent: 'new' -> intent == 'new', expires_at == T + 1h; ttl: '24h', intent: 'x' -> expires_at == T + 24h30m and intent == 'x'}: r = PATCH …/claims/{id}; assert r.status == 200; assert the members as listed; assert paths, target_branch, by, session_id, created_at and state are unchanged; assert no event was written
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] IF the body of PATCH …/claims/{id} carries neither ttl nor intent, a ttl that is not a duration string, is shorter than 1 second or exceeds [awareness].max_claim_ttl, or an intent that is not a string, is empty or is longer than 2,000 characters, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and leave the claim unchanged
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; the claim reads as before
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_routes_test.go, a table over the bodies {{}; ttl: 'x'; ttl: '0s'; ttl: '25h'; intent: ''; intent of 2,001 characters; intent: 4}: before = GET claim; r = PATCH; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert GET claim == before
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] IF PATCH …/claims/{id} names a claim that is released, fulfilled, expired, or stored as active but past its expires_at, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and leave the claim unchanged
   → HTTP 409 with error_type claim_not_active
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_routes_test.go, a table over claims in the states {released, fulfilled, expired by the expiry run, active with expires_at one second ago}: r = PATCH …/claims/{id} {ttl: '1h'}; assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'claim_not_active'; assert the stored expires_at is unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-7.6] WHEN a permitted caller sends DELETE …/claims/{id} for an active claim, THE parleyd SHALL set the claim's state to released and emit parley.claim.release in the same transaction
   → HTTP 204 with an empty body; the claim reads with state released; one event parley.claim.release with resource_type claim, resource_id the id, the caller as actor and metadata {paths}
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real event log on SQLite
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_routes_test.go: r = DELETE …/claims/{id}; assert r.status == 204; assert len(r.body) == 0; assert GET …/claims/{id} .state == 'released'; ev = last event; assert ev.type == 'parley.claim.release'; assert ev.resource_id == id; assert ev.metadata == {paths: ['api/**']}; assert GET …/activity?paths=api/** .claims == []
   ```
1. [REQ-7.7] WHEN a permitted caller sends DELETE …/claims/{id} for a claim that is not active, THE parleyd SHALL change nothing and emit nothing
   → HTTP 204 with an empty body; the claim's state is unchanged and the event log has no new event
   Check: unit

### REQ-8: Claim lifetime in the background

**Rationale:** A crashed agent's claim must disappear by itself, a claim must follow the change it led to, and ended claims must not accumulate for ever.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN the claim expiry run fires, once every minute while parleyd runs, THE parleyd SHALL set every claim that is stored as active and whose expires_at is not after the current time to expired and emit one parley.claim.expire for each, the state and its event in one transaction
   → each such claim reads with state expired; one event parley.claim.expire per claim with resource_type claim, resource_id the id, workspace the claim's workspace_slug, actor system and metadata {paths}; a second run emits nothing for the same claims
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real event log on SQLite
   ```
   in internal/awareness/expiry_test.go with a controlled clock: claims A (expires T + 5m), B (expires T + 2h), C (released); set the clock to T + 6m; run the expiry once; assert stored state of A == 'expired'; assert B is active and C released; ev = events of type parley.claim.expire; assert len(ev) == 1; assert ev[0].resource_id == A and ev[0].actor.actor_type == 'system' and ev[0].metadata == {paths: A.paths}; run again; assert len(events of type parley.claim.expire) == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN the index worker reads the parley.change.version event of version 1 of a change that carries a session_id, THE parleyd SHALL set change to that change's number on every claim of the same session that is active, stored on the change's workspace, on the change's target branch and has change null
   → those claims read with change equal to the number; claims of other sessions, on other target branches, not active or already linked are unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_link_test.go: claims A (s1, main), B (s1, release), C (s2, main), D (s1, main, released), E (s1, main, change 3); feed version 1 of change 7 (session s1, target main); pass; assert A.change == 7; assert B.change == null and C.change == null and D.change == null; assert E.change == 3; feed version 2 of change 8 (session s1, main) without its version 1; pass; assert no claim has change 8
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN the index worker reads a parley.change.land or parley.change.abandon event of a change, THE parleyd SHALL set every active claim whose change is that change's number to fulfilled, without emitting an event
   → those claims read with state fulfilled and are absent from activity; a claim linked to the change that is already released or expired keeps its state
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/claim_link_test.go, a table over the events {land, abandon}: claims A (active, change 7), B (released, change 7), C (active, change 9); feed the event for change 7; pass; assert A.state == 'fulfilled'; assert B.state == 'released'; assert C.state == 'active'; assert no parley.claim.* event was written; feed restore(7); pass; assert A.state == 'fulfilled'
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN the maintenance loop runs the task claim_cleanup, THE parleyd SHALL remove every claim that became released, expired or fulfilled 7 days ago or earlier and keep every other claim
   → GET …/claims/{id} of a removed claim answers HTTP 404 with error_type claim_not_found; active claims and claims that ended less than 7 days ago still read
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/awareness/cleanup_test.go with a controlled clock at T: claims A released at T - 7d, B expired at T - 7d - 1s, C fulfilled at T - 8d, D released at T - 7d + 1s, E active and created at T - 30d with expires_at in the future; run the task registered under the name claim_cleanup; assert ids(all stored claims) == [D, E]; assert GET …/claims/{A} is 404 claim_not_found
   ```
1. [REQ-8.5] THE parleyd SHALL read [awareness].default_claim_ttl (duration, default 1h), [awareness].max_claim_ttl (duration, default 24h) and [awareness].max_claims_per_workspace (integer, default 1000) from the configuration and refuse to start when a duration is not positive, default_claim_ttl exceeds max_claim_ttl or max_claims_per_workspace is below 1
   → with no [awareness] section the three defaults apply; an invalid value stops the start with exit status 1 and an error line that names the key
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/awareness/config_test.go, a table over configuration texts {none -> 1h, 24h, 1000; default_claim_ttl = '30m' -> 30m; max_claim_ttl = '0s' -> error naming awareness.max_claim_ttl; default_claim_ttl = '2d' with max_claim_ttl = '24h' -> error naming awareness.default_claim_ttl; max_claims_per_workspace = 0 -> error naming awareness.max_claims_per_workspace; default_claim_ttl = 'soon' -> error naming awareness.default_claim_ttl; an unregistered key awareness.other -> error}: load through the configuration loader with this package's keys registered; assert the values or the error text
   ```
1. [REQ-8.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any claim and any overlap, leave the opening of changes, the recording of versions, pushes, commits, policy evaluation and landing unaffected
   → a change that touches paths another session has claimed, or that overlaps another change, is opened and versioned with the same status and body as without the claim or the overlap
   Check: same as PATH-1

### REQ-9: CLI commands for awareness

**Rationale:** Agents and scripts ask about activity and manage claims from the shell, and need an exit status that says whether something overlaps.

   → one JSON document on stdout and exit status 0; a hub error is printed on stderr as received with exit status 1
   Check: unit

   in internal/cli/activity_test.go and internal/cli/change_overlaps_test.go, against an httptest server that records requests, a table {['activity', 'demo', '--paths', 'api/**,docs/**'] -> GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/activity with paths == 'api/**,docs/**' and no other parameter; the same with --target release --since <sha> --exclude-session s1 --exclude-change 4 -> the five parameters; ['change', 'overlaps', 'demo', '7'] -> GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/7/overlaps}: assert method, path and query; assert stdout is the served body indented by 2 spaces; assert exit == 0; with the server answering 404 change_not_found assert exit == 1 and the envelope on stderr
   ```

[REQ-9.2] WHERE --fail-on-overlap is given to parley activity or parley change overlaps, THE parley CLI SHALL print the response body first and then, when changes or claims of the activity answer holds an item, or items of the overlaps answer holds an item, report condition_not_met on stderr and exit with status 3
   → exit status 3 with the result on stdout and an envelope with error_type condition_not_met on stderr when something overlaps; exit status 0 when the lists are empty; without the flag exit status 0 in both cases
   Check: unit

   in internal/cli/activity_test.go and internal/cli/change_overlaps_test.go, a table over the served bodies {activity with changes [x] and claims [] -> 3; changes [] and claims [y] -> 3; changes [] and claims [] and landed [z] -> 0; overlaps with items [x] -> 3; overlaps with items [] -> 0} with the flag, and the first and fourth rows without the flag -> 0: assert exit; assert stdout is the body in every row; for exit 3 assert stderr.json.error.error_type == 'condition_not_met' and stderr.json.error.code == 0

1. [REQ-9.3] WHEN a user runs parley claim create, parley claim list, parley claim renew or parley claim release with valid arguments, THE parley CLI SHALL send for create POST …/claims with paths (the comma list split into an array), intent and, when their flags are given, target_branch, ttl and session_id; for list GET …/claims with state, session_id, path, limit and cursor from the flags given; for renew PATCH …/claims/<id> with ttl from --ttl or else 1h; for release DELETE …/claims/<id>; and print the response body, or {} for release

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: Two agents meet on one file and each is told about the other

1. **agent** opens change 1 with POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes from a branch that edits api/handler.go
2. **agent** a second agent runs parley claim create demo --paths 'api/**' --intent 'rework handlers' --session <its session>
3. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/claims and prints the answer
4. **parleyd** stores the claim, emits parley.claim.create and answers 201 with the claim and an activity that lists change 1
5. **agent** the second agent opens change 2 from a branch that also edits api/handler.go, naming its session
6. **parleyd** opens change 2 as it would without the claim and the overlap, and answers 201
7. **parleyd** the index worker reads the version events, records the files of both changes, sets change 2 on the claim and emits one parley.change.overlap on each change
8. **agent** the first agent runs parley change overlaps demo 1 --fail-on-overlap
9. **parley CLI** prints the list with the entry for change 2, reports condition_not_met and exits 3

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI command tree, parleyd HTTP server with its middleware, access component, change routes and change store, event log, awareness index worker running as background work, git wrapper on a real repository, transactional store on SQLite

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with an empty data directory
- a workspace demo cloned from a local origin served by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest, with the branches feat-a and feat-b pushed to the hub, each one commit on main that edits api/handler.go
- two users of the owning organization, each with an API key and one session on demo

**End state:**

- the claim reads with state active and change 2
- GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/1/overlaps holds one entry with change.number 2, paths ['api/handler.go'] and count 1, and the overlaps of change 2 hold change 1
- the event log holds exactly two parley.change.overlap events, one with resource_id '1' naming change 2 and one with resource_id '2' naming change 1, and one parley.claim.create
- parley change overlaps demo 1 --fail-on-overlap exits 3 with the list on stdout
- the POST that opened change 2 answered 201

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/awareness_test.go: hub = startHub(t); demo with feat-a and feat-b; c1 = POST /changes {source: {branch: 'feat-a'}, session_id: sA} as user A; assert c1.status == 201; poll GET …/activity?paths=api/** until numbers(changes) == [1] (at most 10 s); out = runCLI as user B ('claim', 'create', 'demo', '--paths', 'api/**', '--intent', 'rework handlers', '--session', sB); assert out.exit == 0; cl = json(out.stdout); assert numbers(cl.activity.changes) == [1]; c2 = POST /changes {source: {branch: 'feat-b'}, session_id: sB} as user B; assert c2.status == 201; poll GET /events/log filtered to parley.change.overlap until it holds 2 items (at most 10 s); assert the two resource ids are {'1', '2'} and each metadata.with.number is the other; assert GET …/claims/{cl.claim.id} .change == 2; o = runCLI as user A ('change', 'overlaps', 'demo', '1', '--fail-on-overlap'); assert o.exit == 3; assert json(o.stdout).items[0].change.number == 2 and .count == 1
```

### PATH-2: A crashed agent's claim expires and is removed

1. **agent** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/claims with paths ['docs/**'] and ttl 5m, then stops
2. **parleyd** stores the claim with expires_at five minutes later and emits parley.claim.create
3. **parleyd** six minutes later the claim expiry run sets the claim to expired and emits parley.claim.expire
4. **agent** another agent sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/activity?paths=docs/** and receives no claim
5. **parleyd** seven days later the maintenance loop runs claim_cleanup and removes the claim

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd HTTP server with its middleware, claim store on SQLite, claim expiry background work, maintenance loop with the claim_cleanup task, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a controlled clock
- a workspace demo and a user with an API key who can read it

**End state:**

- after the clock passed expires_at and the expiry ran, the claim reads with state expired and activity for docs/** has an empty claims list
- the event log holds one parley.claim.create and one parley.claim.expire for the claim's id
- after the clock moved 7 days further and a maintenance pass ran, GET …/claims/{id} answers 404 claim_not_found

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/awareness_test.go: hub = startHub(t, clock); r = POST /workspaces/demo/claims {paths: ['docs/**'], intent: 'write docs', ttl: '5m'}; id = r.json.claim.id; assert ids(GET …/activity?paths=docs/** .claims) == [id]; clock.advance(6m); hub.runClaimExpiry(); assert GET …/claims/{id} .state == 'expired'; assert GET …/activity?paths=docs/** .claims == []; assert types(GET /events/log for resource claim/id) == ['parley.claim.create', 'parley.claim.expire']; clock.advance(7d); hub.runMaintenancePass(); assert GET …/claims/{id} .status == 404
```

### 1. Index changes by touched file from the event log (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 1.3 Register this package's schema steps with the store of package 03: indexed changes (workspace, number, target branch, phase in flight, landed or out, landed commit and time, session), their files (workspace, number, path), announced pairs, and the worker's position

### 4. Answer the activity query (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Depends on:** 2

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the activity behaviours to internal/awareness/activity_test.go and the glob table to internal/awareness/glob_test.go, with a real repository for target_sha and for a commit since, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add the claim table to this package's schema steps and a claim store with insert and the query for claims that are active and not past expires_at on a workspace and target branch; later tasks add the routes on top of it
- 4.3 Add the glob test for two globs: take each glob's text before its first asterisk as its literal prefix and answer yes when either glob, matched with the path-glob matcher of package 06, matches the other's literal prefix
- 4.4 Parse the query: paths from repeated parameters and comma lists together, each glob validated (1 to 255 characters, no leading slash), 1 to 50 globs; since as exactly 40 hexadecimal characters or an RFC 3339 timestamp, defaulting to 24 hours before the request on the replaceable clock; exclude_change as a positive integer; answer 400 invalid_request for each violation and for a commit the repository does not hold
- 4.5 Resolve target_branch from the target parameter or the default branch of the workspace acted on, and target_sha through the git wrapper, null when the branch does not exist
- 4.6 Build changes from the index: in-flight changes on the target branch with a file matching any glob, as overlap entries over their matching files, ordered by count descending and then number ascending
- 4.7 Build claims from the claim store with the glob test, newest first
- 4.8 Build landed from the index: landed changes on the target branch with a matching file, newest first, selected by landed_at for a timestamp and by the landed commit not being reachable from since for a commit id, cut to 100, each with number, ref, title, landed_sha, landed_at, session_id and its matching files cut to 100
- 4.9 Apply exclude_session and exclude_change to all three lists
- 4.10 Register GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/activity with the scope changes:read and the access need read, and keep the function that builds the answer callable with an extra claim id to leave out, for claim creation
